closed_findings.producer_result: Public chain and exact current receipt/commitment transaction binding are compared through a public-only read before the expected-binding map read.
A fixed owner-private O_EXCL/O_NOFOLLOW reservation spans create or recovery; a loser denies before namespace inspection.
Failure cleanup receives only the failing transaction owned-name to transaction-ID to inode/device map; no namespace-wide deletion exists.
Cleanup performs atomic no-replace rename to transaction quarantine before identity verification and never unlinks or renames after stat.
Manifest oneOf branches bind g3_required false to 8 grades/final 24 and true to 12 grades/final 28.
G3 false exact pin, record, artifact, authority, and grade sets exclude every G3 path; G3 true requires all exact G3 paths.
Sanitized commitment instances and schema use r6-data-quality-blind-map-commitment-v6.
Leak scan returns ERROR/DENY for every oversized, unreadable, symlinked, special, or racy entry instead of PASS.
Leak traversal is descriptor-relative O_NOFOLLOW with before/open/after/name identity continuity and never follows private-map symlinks.
Every fixed source, chain, map, commitment, receipt, lock, stage, and scan read checks an exact maximum before allocation.
Maintained G3 probes cover pending, noncountable, missing, digest-mismatched, and authority-reference-mismatched cases before map read.
The v4 cross-record/nested probes, map uniqueness/order probes, conditional manifest probes, chronology barriers, and reviewed cases are restored.
Dead seal, verify_seal, and _name_identity helpers are removed; active identity/hash paths are directly tested.

expected_benefit: A future separately pinned chain cannot read a private map under the wrong transaction, cannot omit conditional G3 authority, and cannot silently pass incomplete leak or transaction evidence.
observed_problem: The exact OPEN-v5 review found six critical, four high, two medium and one low defect across opening order, concurrent transactions, cleanup identity, G3 schema/runtime parity, commitment discrimination, bounded reads, leak scanning and regression coverage.
